plan.voiceover:
[conversational] Those viral ChatGPT slash commands? They're not built in. Not even close.

They're just plain text ChatGPT reads as instructions. So write your own, and they work far more reliably.

[confident] Step 1: write the definition. Like this: "/exploded equals: create a labeled exploded-view illustration of the object, parts separated, white background." Add one for /anatomy and /cutaway.

Step 2: click your profile icon, Settings, Personalization. Make sure Enable customization is ON, paste it into Custom Instructions, and save. On phone, it's Settings, then Customize ChatGPT.

Step 3: start a new chat and type "/exploded mechanical keyboard."

[whispers] For one topic only, use a Project: the three dots, then Project settings. Only project instructions apply there.

[serious] Catch: Free gets 1,500 characters, free image generation is capped with no official number, and labels can be wrong. If it ignores you, tell it to follow the matching definition.

Which command would you build first?

Send this to the friend who copies prompts from reel captions.

manual_request.what: Screen-record chatgpt.com in dark mode with the three command definitions already saved in Custom Instructions. Shot 1: click New chat. Shot 2: type '/exploded mechanical keyboard' and press send. Shot 3: keep recording until the generated labeled exploded-view image has fully appeared, including any caption. Optional shot 4: the same with '/cutaway' plus an object. Vertical crop or full-window capture is fine.
manual_request.why: The generated image changes every time and cannot be faked believably. Viewers need to see the real result.

pick.angle: Those 'secret ChatGPT commands' going viral aren't built in. Here's how to make real shortcuts that work every time.
pick.why: The 'secret commands' format is proven: @insideraix got 4.2M views and 115k likes in 2 days (29s). Related command-style reels also pull huge numbers: @cindiezhu 13.2M views and 7.1k comments, @as.digital.deals 37k comments. It is easy to teach in 3 steps (write the shortcut, save it, trigger it), and the 'not real commands' claim is true and checkable.

research.tool: ChatGPT Custom Instructions (Settings > Personalization) and Project instructions (Projects > Project settings)

WEB/DESKTOP, global shortcuts: click your profile icon, then Settings, then Personalization. Make sure 'Enable customization' is ON. Paste your command definitions into the 'Custom Instructions' field and save.
PHONE (iOS/Android), global shortcuts: open Settings, then 'Customize ChatGPT'. Make sure 'Enable customization' is ON. Paste your command definitions into the 'Custom Instructions' field.

OPTION B, shortcuts for one topic only: open 'Projects' in the left sidebar and create a new project with a name. Open the project's more options menu (•••), then 'Project settings', and paste the command definitions into the instructions. Alternatively, open the project's three-dots menu and choose 'Add instructions' or 'Edit instructions'. Project instructions apply only to chats inside that project.

facts: Custom instructions are 'available on all plans on Web, Desktop, iOS, and Android' (OpenAI Help Center).

Web/Desktop path per OpenAI: Settings > Personalization > toggle 'Enable customization' ON > enter text in the 'Custom Instructions' field. Mobile path: Settings > 'Customize ChatGPT' > same toggle and field.
OpenAI says custom-instruction updates apply immediately across all chats, including existing conversations.

Limits: 'Free and Go users can save up to 1,500 characters'; Plus, Pro, Enterprise, Business and Education users can save up to 5,000 (OpenAI Help Center). A third-party site dates the paid-tier increase to July 15, 2026.

The OpenAI Help Center currently describes one 'Custom Instructions' field. Older guides, and Tom's Guide, describe two boxes: 'What would you like ChatGPT to know about you?' and 'How would you like ChatGPT to respond?'.
Projects: OpenAI Help says to select the more options menu (•••), then 'Project settings', to add project instructions.
Inside a project, global custom instructions are not applied. The Help Center table says 'Not available (only project instructions)' for chats in projects.
Projects opened to Free users in September 2025 (per findskill.ai and Tech.co). Free allows 5 files per project, and Plus allows 25 (Yahoo Tech).

On Free, 'image generation... have separate usage limits' (OpenAI Free Tier FAQ, as quoted by aifreeapi.com). OpenAI publishes no numeric daily image cap for consumer plans (felloai.com, aifreeapi.com, whizi.io, Oct 2026).
The image generator is ChatGPT Images 2.5, the default since 8 September 2026. It is available on every plan including Free. Thinking Mode is paid-only (felloai.com, secondary source).

Independent explainers confirm /anatomy, /exploded, /cutaway and similar are NOT built-in. Artea says there is no hidden slash-command menu for image generation. The GitHub repo says they are 'not official ChatGPT slash commands'. A note.com article says there are no 100 hidden official commands.
These words work only because ChatGPT reads them as plain instructions (Artea). Naming the components in the prompt gives much better results (Artea).
do_not_claim: Do NOT say /anatomy, /exploded view or /cutaway are secret, hidden or built-in ChatGPT commands. They are community prompt conventions with no official documentation.
Do NOT write the command as '/exploded view' with a space. A space breaks the one-word trigger. Use /exploded or /explodedview. The reel's '/cutaway' and '/anatomy' are fine as custom words.
Do NOT promise they work on any object or any photo, or with 'perfect' accuracy. Results depend on the subject and prompt, and labels or parts can be wrong.

Do NOT say 'unlimited free'. The reel's 'completely free' is only half true: image generation is free but capped on Free, with no official number. Old '3 per day' and '2-3 per day' figures are unofficial or outdated estimates.
Do NOT say Projects are Plus-only, or that Custom Instructions are two boxes on every app. Older articles still say both.

Do NOT claim a typed '/' opens a native command menu in ChatGPT. The reel and the unverified claim that 'commands are in the caption' give no official mechanism. Check the live UI before showing any popup.

Do NOT claim global Custom Instructions combine with project instructions inside a Project. OpenAI's table says only project instructions apply there. A secondary site (ai-toolbox) says the opposite, so avoid the claim.
Do NOT claim shortcuts work 'every time' or 'guaranteed'. LLMs can still skip or misread instructions, so say 'far more reliable' instead.
Do not use the reel's commands as exact strings. The caption shows only names, not prompts, and the reel gives no verified prompt text.
criticism: ChatGPT has no true slash-command system. These are text conventions, and the model may misinterpret or ignore them (Artea, GitHub repo disclaimer).
Free users have only 1,500 characters, so only a few detailed definitions fit.
Free image generation has a separate cap with no published number. Users report hitting the 'free plan limit' message.
Global Custom Instructions apply to ALL chats. Long shortcut text can clutter unrelated chats, so a Project may be better for visuals.

Memory/privacy: instructions are stored in your account. Don't put sensitive data in them (customgpt.ai advice). Project data can be used for model improvement if 'Improve the model for everyone' is ON (futurefactors.ai).
Image accuracy: labeled technical diagrams from an image model can contain wrong parts or garbled text. This is an inference, not directly sourced; show it with a real test.
